brief_rationale: The trajectory has no serious responsibility-chain error: the doctor recognized the post-induction stage, stopped old aspirin/heparin use, gave urgent warning signs, arranged obstetric follow-up, and obtained patient receipt. However, there are minor/moderate responsibility-chain omissions: post-induction red flags did not cover dizziness/weakness/syncope, thyroid medication was not specifically handled as “do not self-stop/change; follow original prescriber,” and the fetal screening/ultrasound results were not fully classified for genetic counseling review. Under the frozen rubric, any minor in-chain error caps the score at 2 despite later teach-back and useful follow-up planning.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode was traceable and largely executable for aspirin/heparin, urgent symptoms, and obstetric follow-up, but closure was premature because important minimum duties remained incomplete, especially explicit thyroid-medication handling and full post-induction red-flag coverage.
closure_assessment.label: premature_closure

high_order_assessment.explanation: The doctor showed some verification awareness for ANA and future pregnancy planning, but did not complete the case-specific verification work: no ENA/antiphospholipid-type follow-up was specified, thyroid medication/labs were not concretely verified, and fetal screening/ultrasound results were not fully reviewed for genetic counseling.

The patient had not actually continued or restarted aspirin, heparin, or pregnancy-support medications after discharge, so the specific repair scenario of already-executed medication error was not triggered.

important_non_chain_defect_assessment.explanation: The decisive problems are responsibility-chain omissions rather than a separate non-chain defect. Communication was generally supportive and the plan was partly executable.
